- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is falling.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or mixed; apply downward bias to first 5–7 forecast points.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply smoothing or lagged correction to avoid overreaction.
- Mean reversion is evident in 30-day forecasts: model frequently fails to capture price returning to historical mean after volatility; apply mean-reversion adjustment if recent 18-day average is significantly above or below forecast.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33) triggers model lag; delay or reduce forecast adjustment until sentiment stabilizes or confirms direction.
